text:
maya: FYI adding a new intake — vendor 'Opal' 17B (float16). Requesting quick prioritization for bring-up. primary asks: perf (latency/throughput), quant friendliness, eval quality on chat and code prompts.

raj: :eyes: can you paste the basic perf expectations and target SLOs? also what business signal would justify a dedicated slot?

maya: Target SLOs: p50 <= 110ms @ 4k context on A100-80GB; p99 <= 600ms. Throughput target 1200 tokens/s per GPU (batched). Business signal: outperforms existing 13B on instruction-following OR reduces token cost by >15% with comparable quality.

leo: Quick triage notes from prelim run: runs fine FP16, but KV-cache growth at long context is ~12% higher than our baseline; attention kernel path triggers fallback for seq>8192 — that might hurt tail latencies.

ian: Suggest immediate gating checks: quality smoke (10 prompts), hallucination heuristics, RLHF sensitivity, and a basic quantization smoke to int8. I can own the quant experiments this sprint if we slot it.

raj: For prioritization scoring, propose we use the usual rubric: model utility, infra cost delta, quantizability, and rollout risk. Want a quick calc now?

maya: go for it. I ran a lightweight scorecard, rough numbers below. Can we validate/adjust?

maya: ```
weights = {"utility": 0.4, "cost_delta": 0.25, "quantizability": 0.2, "risk": 0.15}
scores = {"utility": 7, "cost_delta": 6, "quantizability": 5, "risk": 4}
priority = sum(weights[k]*scores[k] for k in scores)  # => 6.05 (out of 10)
```

leo: That feels fair as a baseline. My note: downgrade quantizability to 4 unless int8 smoke passes — KV-cache patterns may make 4-bit tricks less effective.

ian: I'll run a 4-bit and int8 pass on a single GPU today. ETA end of day. If int8 keeps <7% tok quality drop on eval set, we can boost quantizability to 7.

maya: Roadmap alignment note: product asked for an improved code-generation mid-sized model before end of quarter. If Opal 17B shows superior code completion latencies, this might bump priority.

raj: Ok action items: 1) ian runs quant smokes (owner: ian) — due EOD today. 2) leo to run 100-example quality smoke and hallucination checks — due tomorrow morning. 3) maya to produce short perf-run config and cost delta calc on Dedicated pool — due tomorrow. 4) if all green, schedule canary next week.

leo: +1 on that plan. tagging @ops-bot to check capacity for a single-GPU canary slot next week.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Canary capacity check queued. Current Dedicated free slots next week: Mon(2), Tue(0), Wed(1), Thu(3), Fri(1). Requested: 1 GPU.

maya: Great — let's tentatively target Wed for canary if EOD smokes look good.

raj: One more: add an eval slice for regression on our anchor prompts (support chat + code). If quality regression >2% on any anchor, automatic rollback.

ian: running now, will post results in the thread.

ian: quick update: int8 pass done — token-level BLEU drop ~3.2% on code set, emscore drop 2.8% on chat. attaching logs in the eval doc (link: https://redwood.internal/evals/opal-17b-smoke).

leo: thanks. given that, ian: please run a lighter 4-bit ilql pass — maybe we get better cost win with acceptable quality.

ian: 4-bit run queued. if that looks good, we can proceed to canary but with immediate fallback policy (route 5% traffic to baseline).

maya: Sounds good. tagging this as "pending quant verification". We'll reconvene in the weekly model-review if still open.

raj: final thought: if 4-bit fails, we still might prioritize for roadmap if utility on code tasks is >8.5/10. otherwise deprioritize.

ian: 4-bit results posted: quality drop ~1.1% on code, cost delta estimated -18% tokens cost. updating scorecard to quantizability=7 -> new priority ~6.6.

maya: ok locking in canary Wed, owner ian. I'll add rollout policy and monitor alerts in Redwood Console.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Canary created for Wed 09:00 UTC, 1 GPU dedicated slot. Alert hooks: latency-p99, model-regression-rate, token-cost-surge.

leo: :thumbsup: I'll prep the short eval deck for the weekly review.

maya: Thanks team — will close the intake and move to bring-up flow once canary passes.

ian: leaving final note: documented quant configs in the experiment doc. link: https://redwood.internal/quant/opal-17b-configs

maya: closing loop — moving thread to "bring-up" board.
